name: 5S Audit Checklist
description: A printable 5S audit for walking one work area and scoring Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardize and Sustain.

items.text: Remove items not used in this area in the last month
Red-tag any item whose need is unclear
items.note: Write the item, date, name of the person tagging it and the reason on the tag.

items.text: Move red-tagged items to the marked red-tag holding area
Set a holding period, such as 30 days, and dispose of unclaimed items
Clear broken tools, scrap and expired materials from the area
Keep only the stock needed for the current shift or job
Give every tool and item one fixed home
Store the most-used items closest to the point of use
Mount hand tools on shadow boards with an outline for each tool
items.note: An empty outline shows at a glance what is missing or not put back.

items.text: Label shelves, bins, drawers and cabinets with their contents
Mark walkways, work cells and storage spots with floor tape or paint
Set min/max levels on stock locations so shortages show
Clean floors, benches and machines, including under and behind them
Check for leaks, loose parts and wear while cleaning
items.note: Cleaning is also an inspection. Note oil drips, frayed cables and loose guards.

items.text: Find the sources of dirt, dust and spills and fix them
Keep cleaning supplies stocked in a labeled spot in the area
Post a cleaning schedule that names who cleans what and when
Take a photo of the area at its best and post it as the standard
Use the same label style, colors and floor markings across all areas
items.note: One color code site-wide, such as yellow for walkways, avoids confusion when staff move between areas.

items.text: Write short one-page instructions for daily 5S tasks
Add 5S tasks to shift start-up or shutdown routines
Make sure everyone in the area can explain the standard
Schedule regular audits and post the dates
Post audit scores where the team can see them
Assign an owner and due date to every finding
items.note: A finding with no name next to it rarely gets fixed. Check last audit's actions first.

items.text: Train new staff in the area standard during their first week
Review results with the team and agree on the next fix
Check that exits, fire extinguishers and electrical panels are clear
Look for trip hazards, missing guards and damaged equipment
Confirm required PPE is available and in use
Area: ____  Date: ____
Score (0–5) per S: Sort ____  Set ____  Shine ____  Standardize ____  Sustain ____
items.note: 0 = not started, 3 = in place but not consistent, 5 = fully in place and maintained.

items.text: Total score (out of 25): ____  Previous score: ____
Top three actions, owner and due date: ____
Auditor: ____  Area owner: ____  Next audit date: ____

faq.a: Sort (Seiri), Set in Order (Seiton), Shine (Seiso), Standardize (Seiketsu) and Sustain (Shitsuke). Do them in that order. There is no point labeling a shelf for items you are about to throw out, or cleaning around clutter.

6S adds Safety to the five S's. Some sites treat it as a separate step, checking for trip hazards, blocked exits, missing guards and PPE. Others fold safety checks into each S. If your site uses 6S, add a Safety row to the score sheet.

faq.q: How often should you do a 5S audit?
faq.a: Many sites audit each area weekly while 5S is new, then monthly once scores are steady. Short daily checks by the people who work in the area, plus a monthly audit by someone from outside it, catch more than either one alone.

faq.q: What is a red tag in 5S?
faq.a: A red tag marks an item whose need is in doubt during Sort. The tag records what the item is, who tagged it, the date and why. Tagged items go to a holding area for a set time. If no one claims them, they are moved, sold, recycled or scrapped.
